recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If OO later wants a different taxonomy or criteria for device-related resources, update the Device module and Device page together through a new work-group decision rather than expanding this resolved clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-47887 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification OO R6 clarification request for Device Boundaries and Relationships asking what made the listed resources device-related and requesting descriptive text for the list that had started with 'These are the device related resources'.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by 3cf635fa2b606d038462a683a53338e39b3f30e3, which explicitly listed FHIR-47887 and changed source/device/device-introduction.xml from the unclear ballot sentence to a paragraph saying several resources can represent device-related events, requests, or definitions, followed by usage descriptions. Later Device edits retained that clarification while fixing formatting and external incubator links.
additional_context: Device is active in source/fhir.ini, and Confluence OO/HCP minutes show FHIR-47887 was approved with exact wording delegated to HCP/editors. The current Device module provides broader categories and tables for device-related resources, matching the HCP decision to keep resource pages focused on critical boundaries while moving broader relationship detail to the module. FHIR-47886 is a same-change-family issue for the separated workflow-resource bullets but was not separately decided here.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current resource page already explains the purpose of the list as device-related events, requests, or definitions, describes the listed resources, and links to the broader Device module; adding more text would be redundant and could create maintenance drift.

related_jiras.note: Asked why DeviceRequest/DeviceDispense and SupplyRequest/SupplyDelivery were paired; the same Device BNR edit family split and described those bullets, but this run only audited FHIR-47887.
